L'Équipe, c'est le quotidien sportif de: L'Équipe is France's reference sports daily — but it's also a catalogue of 50 podcasts covering every sport, from the NBA to cycling by way of F1, European football and even esports. Dozens of formats produced by sports journalists who have made analysis their trademark.
Pour cet épisode spécial, Alex et Lolo o: For this special episode, Alex and Lolo listened to everything. Really everything. Here are the three formats that genuinely stand out:
Le podcast basket de L'Équipe. NBA, Euro: L'Équipe's basketball podcast. NBA, EuroLeague, the French national team. It covers the XXL schedule, mental fatigue, Wembanyama, LeBron — and you understand the NBA without needing a PhD in statistics.
Le décodeur des grandes ligues européenn: The decoder of Europe's big leagues. Tactics, club business models, underlying dynamics. Dry, solid, rare. A podcast that treats football as a serious subject.
Les jeunes talents et les tendances qu'o: The young talents and trends nobody has seen coming yet. A forward-looking format run by people who really know what they're talking about — and who are often right before everyone else.
Le verdict de départ était une question: The starting verdict was a simple question: can a big sports outlet make good podcasts? The answer, after 50 episodes, is yes — and that's more surprising than it seems. These formats do something that's becoming rare in 2026: they don't just repeat the news, they analyse it, contextualise it and build a real point of view.
Step Back est la meilleure surprise — la: Step Back is the best surprise — the NBA told with a depth you won't find anywhere else in French. Big 5 and L'Avenir leur appartient confirm that L'Équipe's journalists have understood that audio deserves better than a match summary. A small drawback: across 50 podcasts, quality is very uneven — some formats don't really justify their existence. But the best are genuinely excellent.
« Ces podcasts font ce qui devient rare: “These podcasts do what's becoming rare — they don't repeat the news, they explain it. And sometimes they teach you why certain teams play as if they'd discovered football at a birthday party. It's serious audio journalism.” — Alex & Lolo
